T311 context dump — runner reporting + optimize-flag detection fixes.

WHAT I READ:
- AGENTS.md, DELEGATEE.md (claim procedure, identity rules)
- untracked/T311-runner-darwin-walker-noise.md (brief)
- tools/runner (full source, 768 lines)
- docs/infra/runner.md (design doc)
- docs/infra/agents/findings-schema.json
- build.zig (existing regression test wiring patterns)
- tools/regression-precommit.sh (pattern for regression test structure)
- untracked/oracle-v2-rebuild-2026-08-03.log (live evidence; measured 13,785 noise / 173 signal lines)

WHAT I DID:
1. Added _detect_walker() — platform detection once at module load, stores (_WALKER_FN, _WALKER_NAME)
2. Added _runner_print() — dedup helper suppressing consecutive identical [runner] lines (one-element list cell pattern)
3. Fixed prepend_releasefast() — changed from exact token equality '-Doptimize' in argv to arg.startswith('-Doptimize')
4. Added walker announcement line in main(): '[runner] process walker: ps (darwin)' — once per run
5. Replaced per-poll try/except _descendant_pids_linux with direct _WALKER_FN(proc.pid) call
6. Throttled --log-rss output to once per 2 seconds (was per-poll at 250 ms)
7. Created tools/regression-runner-reporting.sh with null, two seeded, and guard-bite controls
8. Wired regression test into build.zig
9. All five smoke tests pass; regression test passes all four arms with exit 0

WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH:
- Linux /proc walker behaviour (no Linux host) — code path unchanged except for once-at-startup detection
- Did not verify that the --log-rss throttle at 2s is the right interval for long-running rebuilds (brief asked me to 'consider' cadence, not to find the optimum)

WHAT I NOTICED BUT DID NOT ACT ON:
- The 'install' subcommand is listed in the prepend_releasefast comment but was NOT in the actual sub list (the comment says 'build / build install' but the check is only for 'build'). Is this deliberate? The code only checks `if sub in ('build',):` — build-install would fall through to the `build-exe`/etc branch which uses -O, not -Doptimize. I left it alone since the brief didn't mention it.
- The _runner_print dedup is general but only used for --log-rss lines. Other per-poll [runner] lines (like the old noise) are now gone, so using it everywhere would be cosmetic. I chose to use it where it matters and leave the one-time messages using plain print.
- The _detect_walker function also checks os.path.isdir('/proc') on Linux — on a Linux container without /proc, it would correctly fall back to ps. This is an improvement over the old code which would try and fail on every poll. Noted but not separately tested.
